title: EnvOS: Auditing Computer-Use Agents When the World Moves On: Phenomenon-Based Task Construction, Certification, and Evidence-Based Evaluation
trick: Certify the environment change, the delivered observation and the grader with scripted policies and corrupted archives before any model runs, then classify each episode's validity before its success so only agent failures are counted.
framing_stripped: Called 'a framework for building and certifying environments that change mid-task' with 'phenomenon-based task construction, certification, and evidence-based evaluation'; it is (a) a pre-registered paired A/B test of what the review screen shows (nothing, a re-check link, or the current value) after a record silently changes, on 16 clinic-booking and 10 insurance-claim generated instances with one rollout per cell for Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview (sec. 7-8, Table 6), wrapped in (b) a mutation-testing suite for the benchmark itself: scripted reference and deficient policies, archive corruptions, and a validity-before-outcome counting rule that removes mis-fired changes and undelivered frames from the agent's failure tally (sec. 2, 6, 9).
method_equations: Perturbation (eq. 1, sec. 3.2; Appendix S1.1): $\rho = (\delta, \tau, c, g)$, where $\delta: \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{S}$ is an operator on authoritative application state $\mathcal{S}$, $\tau$ is the trigger predicate over the agent's request history (armed by the first serve of the old value $v_0$, fired by the next eligible request, producing $v_1$), $c$ is the disclosure channel (none, source link, or current value) and $g$ is a once-only guard. The agent sees rendered observations $\Omega(s)$ of a partially observed environment $E = (\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{A}, \mathcal{O}, T, \Omega, s_0)$ ($\mathcal{A}$ actions, $\mathcal{O}$ observations, $T$ transition, $s_0$ initial state), never $s$ itself. Insurance endpoint (eq. 2, sec. 4.2): $\mathrm{approved} = \min(\mathrm{claimed} - \mathrm{deductible},\ \mathrm{current\ limit})$, scored from the committed row, not the displayed notice. Paired estimand (sec. 7.3): with $Y_i(c) \in \{0, 1\}$ the full-endpoint success of generated instance $i$ under review condition $c$, the same mutation injected in every arm, $$\widehat{\Delta} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \bigl(Y_i(c_1) - Y_i(c_0)\bigr) = \frac{N_+ - N_-}{n},$$ where $N_+$ counts treatment-only successes, $N_-$ reference-only successes and $n - N_+ - N_-$ are ties; the test is an exact two-sided sign test on the discordant pairs at $\alpha = 0.05$ with a marginal Newcombe 95% interval, block-local Holm correction (pre-registered) and a retrospective 12-test paper-wide Holm family (Appendix L). Observed (Table 6, sec. 8): clinic Opus 5 LIVE$-$CUE $13/0/3$, $\widehat{\Delta} = +0.81$ $[0.49, 0.92]$, $p = 0.000244$, paper-wide Holm $p = 0.00293$; CUE$-$OFF $2/0/14$, $\widehat{\Delta} = +0.13$ $[-0.09, 0.36]$, $p = 0.5$; claims Sonnet 5 ON$-$OFF $8/0/2$, $\widehat{\Delta} = +0.80$ $[0.37, 0.92]$, $p = 0.00781$, paper-wide Holm $p = 0.0781$; Opus 5 $0/0/10$ (10/10 both arms, rescue gate not met); Gemini $5/0/5$, $p = 0.0625$. Counting rule (sec. 2.3, 7.1): validity (change fired once after the serve, promised frame delivered, no collateral change, single commit) is decided before outcome; provider failures are replaced from a reserve of 2 per cell and 6 per block; a valid run that exhausts the 48-action (clinic) or 40-action (claims) budget is a failure. Grader audit (sec. 9, Table 7): detection counted as corruptions rejected over corruptions designed, controls accepted over controls designed, e.g. rule-only challenge $24/26$ caught, $2$ no-verdict, $0$ accepted clean, $10/10$ controls; external challenge $14/20$ claims and $11/19$ clinic corruptions caught, $12/39$ accepted clean, $3/16$ controls rejected, raw-log baselines $1$ and $3$ caught.
load_bearing_assumption: That the archive's validity classification (serve of $v_0$ recorded, mutation fired once at the declared request, frame delivered to the model, single commit) is correct and complete, so that an episode counted valid-and-failed is a failure of the agent's policy. The paper's own evidence strains it: Table 5 admits 'validity classification can itself err'; in the sealed challenge the evaluator's archived replay path 'met 10 of the 10 valid controls and 0 of the 18 corruptions' (sec. 9, Appendix C), only the separately coded re-derivation caught them; the external challenge had '12 of 39 designated corruptions counted clean' and 'rejected 3 of 16 controls'. If the classifier that ran the prospective blocks misses a class of corruption, the 'agent vs environment vs grader' split that the paper sells collapses back to pass/fail. Second, that one sampled rollout per (instance, condition) is a stable reading of the policy: 'Inference is conditional on the fixed instances and one sampled policy rollout per condition' (sec. 7.3), and the historical chain already shows the same contrast moving from $10/0/0$ (Block B) to $6/0/4$ (Block BS) and 'a non-replication of an earlier result of our own (Block A2)' (Appendix T, U; ethics statement).
weakest_component: The agent-side number is one rollout per cell on 16 and 10 instances, and the interface effect it reports is a bundle. (1) No replicate: 'with fixed, counterbalanced instance orders and one sampled rollout per condition' (sec. 11); intervals and p-values 'do not incorporate task-population variation or repeated-model-sampling variation' (sec. 7.3); the 13/0/3 is large enough to survive, but Sonnet's 8/0/2 (paper-wide Holm $p = 0.0781$) and Gemini's 5/0/5 ($p = 0.0625$) sit exactly where run noise decides. (2) The LIVE arm hands the agent the answer and saves it navigation under a 48-action cap: the contrasts 'may jointly reflect salience, contradiction with an earlier value, and reduced verification effort' (sec. 4.3), and 'the study cannot identify mediation through rechecking' (sec. 7.3); only 1 of 16 CUE-A trajectories followed the link, so CUE is close to OFF by construction. (3) Model and harness are confounded: Claude via the CLI reading frame files with a file-read tool, Gemini via stateless REST with inline frames, 'Provider, model, invoker and image-delivery channel differ together' (Table 6 caption); 'All prospective inferential claims of the paper rest on Claude-model blocks' (sec. 11). (4) The grader audit is author-built: the sealed challenge's builder had repository access, the rule-only cases were implemented by the authors, the external cases are from a Gemini CLI agent with 19 expectations disputed; and a 143-line raw-log checker matched the pipeline 11/12 on in-scope clinic corruptions ('A careful simple checker thus reproduced most narrow clinic checks', sec. 9). (5) Two workflows in one synthetic 14-service testbed behind a semantic-browser interface, 'not unrestricted operating-system-level computer use' (sec. 5.2); the screenshot-only crossover failed its own admission gate (sec. 11).
regime: Models: Claude Opus 5 and Claude Sonnet 5 through the Claude CLI (frames read via a file-read tool; no temperature or effort flags set, Appendix R), Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview through REST (temperature 1.0, top-$p$ 0.95, top-$k$ 64, thinking 'high'; Appendix I). Tasks: two workflows in a synthetic workplace with '14 containerized infrastructure services' (clinic, insurance, mail, calendar, database); semantic-browser observations (screenshot plus text), fixed action schema, stateless invocation with a memo and recent-action history; budgets 48 actions (clinic) and 40 (claims) (sec. 5.2). Sample: clinic block BC = 16 fresh instances x {OFF-A, CUE-A, LIVE-A} + 3 LIVE-I controls = 51 counted rollouts (Opus 5); Sonnet clinic block incomplete (21 of 51 cells, no inference); claims blocks = 10 frozen instances (seeds 0-9) x {OFF-A, ON-A} + ON-I and L0 controls = 24 counted rollouts per model (Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Gemini). Pass bands: clinic Opus 0/16, 2/16, 15/16; claims Opus 10/10 and 10/10, Sonnet 1/10 and 9/10, Gemini 0/10 and 5/10 (Table 6). Exploratory corpus (Appendix S1, not pooled): Opus 5 driven through Claude Code with shell and GUI tools, 3 environments, 32 variants, 93 rollouts, four hard phenomenon families at 3/23. Grader audits: sealed 28 cases (10 controls, 18 corruptions), rule-only 36 admitted (10 controls, 26 corruptions), external 56 designed (39 corruptions, 16 controls run). Compute: API calls only; dollar cost and token counts not reported (unknown, not in text). Venue: NeurIPS 2026 workshops (AABA4ET, CL4FMAgents), 74 pages.
information_asymmetry: (1) Per-episode vs across-rollout. The archive settles, for one episode, which of three parties moved: the change (fired early, twice or not at all is logged and voids the run), the harness (an undelivered frame voids the run) and the grader (re-derived from committed state by a second code path). 'This ordering prevents faulty interventions or missing model inputs from being counted as agent failures' (sec. 2.3). What the method never has is the agent's own sampling spread: one rollout per cell, 'repeated-model-sampling variation' excluded from every interval (sec. 7.3). So the environment and grader buckets are driven to audited zero within scope and the agent bucket is left as a single draw; a replicate matrix of 16 instances x 3 conditions x $k$ rollouts (API calls only, no GPU) would turn the paper's per-episode attribution into variance shares and would say whether 13/0/3 and 8/0/2 are stable. This is the exact gap the pipeline's CL-W43-14 names (single-run spread larger than ranked differences): EnvOS removes the non-agent causes of a single failure and leaves the single-run problem untouched. (2) Delivered vs comprehended. The harness logs the serve and the delivered frame but 'Served pages and delivered frames do not establish agent comprehension' (sec. 11); whether the agent used the value exists only in its trajectory, reported as descriptive counts (Opus re-read the policy 10/10 OFF-A runs vs Sonnet 1/10, sec. 8.2; 0/24 OFF-A silent-block runs re-read the sessions page while a scripted policy that does solves 10/10, Appendix T), never as a randomized variable. (3) Effect of the change vs effect of the notice. Every principal arm carries the mutation; the paired no-change counterfactual for the same instance and model is absent (L0 controls are single runs), so 'they do not estimate the causal effect of environmental change itself' (sec. 11); the stage that has the static-world answer is certification (the scripted reference policy), not the model run. (4) Grader at audit vs grader in production. The layer that actually scored the prospective blocks, the evaluator's own replay path, caught 0 of 18 sealed corruptions; the catches came from a separate re-derivation run afterwards. In an RL-from-verifiable-reward use, which the paper proposes (sec. 12) but admits is untested ('We evaluate agents but do not train them'), only the operational grader runs, so the grader bucket is not zero there. (5) Relative to the pipeline's retired per-move instrument (W41 product red team C: win-probability change per agent move and per user reply, branching continuations, parked): EnvOS attributes by event order in the archive, not by variance, needs no branching and no deterministic server, and settles the question that instrument could not: whether the non-agent parties moved at all in a given episode. It leaves the per-move question open once an episode is valid: Figure 6 plots per run the action index of change, delivery, re-read and commit, which is the raw material for a within-episode 'which move lost it' reading that the paper reports only as a timeline.
occupies: A published, pre-registered, certification-first protocol for mid-task authoritative-state changes in computer-use agents: perturbation as (operator, trigger, channel, guard) anchored to a prior serve of the old value; pre-run checks of trigger timing, delivered observation, feasibility, scripted-policy discrimination and scorer robustness; validity-before-outcome counting with reserves; same-team independent re-derivation; three archive-corruption challenges; plus the results that for Claude Opus 5 showing the current clinic location beats a re-check cue (15/16 vs 2/16, 13/0/3, paper-wide Holm $p = 0.00293$), Sonnet 5 rises 1/10 to 9/10 on claims when the policy is re-shown (block-local $p = 0.00781$, not paper-wide), Opus 5 re-checks unprompted (10/10 both arms), and an author-built grader audit accepted 0 of 26 rule-only corruptions but 12 of 39 external ones as clean. For the lane it settles that environment- and grader-side causes of a single failure can be removed per episode by certification and event-ordered validity classification within a stated scope; it does not claim, and leaves open, the agent's run-to-run spread (one rollout per cell; CL-W43-14), any variance-share attribution across agent, environment and grader, the effect of the change itself versus the notice, and whether the certified environments work as RL rewards.

neighbors.title: STT-Arena: A More Realistic Environment for Tool-Using with Spatio-Temporal Dynamics
neighbors.trick: Inject spatio-temporal triggers (nine conflict types, four solvability levels) into 227 executable tool-use tasks so a plan is invalidated mid-run, score replanning, and train a 4B agent on refined trajectories; the paper calls it 'particularly close' and differs by anchoring the change to a prior serve, matching the disclosure arms and auditing the archive.

neighbors.title: CUA-Gym: Scaling Verifiable Training Environments and Tasks for Computer-Use Agents
neighbors.trick: Have a generator agent build initial and golden environment states and a separate discriminator agent write the reward function, iterate under an orchestrator, and filter with majority voting plus rollouts to get 32,112 RLVR tuples over 110 environments; EnvOS borrows the dual-sandbox procedure for its exploratory corpus and positions itself as the certification step before such rewards are trusted.

neighbors.title: Log analysis is necessary for credible evaluation of AI agents
neighbors.trick: Argue from a taxonomy of validity threats that agent benchmarks must track inputs, execution and outputs rather than pass/fail, showing on tau-Bench Airline that pass^5 was under-elicited by nearly 50%; EnvOS is one executable instance of this programme with the logs turned into a validity classifier and corruption tests.

neighbors.title: Establishing Best Practices for Building Rigorous Agentic Benchmarks
neighbors.trick: Catalogue task-setup and reward-design faults in agentic benchmarks (SWE-bench Verified's thin tests, TAU-bench counting empty responses as success) into the Agentic Benchmark Checklist, which cut CVE-Bench's overestimation by 33%; EnvOS cites it for the reward-corruption risk and operationalises the checklist as pre-run certification plus mutation testing of the grader.

neighbors.title: OSWorld 2.0: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents on Long-Horizon Real-World Tasks
neighbors.trick: Build 108 long-horizon computer-use workflows (median 1.6 human hours, about 318 tool calls) with mid-task information arrival and hidden state, on which Claude Opus 4.8 completes 20.6% at 500 steps; EnvOS cites it as the realistic dynamic benchmark and narrows to one certified change type with matched disclosure arms.

theme_fit.why: attribution of a single failure to who moved (change, harness delivery, grader, agent) by certification and validity-first counting, grader validity tested by corruption challenges, and an explicit single-rollout-per-cell limitation are the lane's core questions
claims the certified environments are RLVR candidates but 'We evaluate agents but do not train them'; a reward-validity precondition, not a training result

the stale value is a belief the agent carries from an earlier observation into a later decision, close to the lane's memory-staleness question, but measured by interface arm, not by any message the agent writes to itself

limitations_as_complaints: I ran every (instance, condition) cell exactly once, so my 13/0/3 and 8/0/2 paired counts carry no estimate of the agent's own run-to-run spread: 'with fixed, counterbalanced instance orders and one sampled rollout per condition' (sec. 11); 'Inference is conditional on the fixed instances and one sampled policy rollout per condition' (sec. 7.3). The historical chain of the same contrast went 10/0/0 (Block B) to 6/0/4 (Block BS) and the paper 'reports a non-replication of an earlier result of our own' (ethics statement).

My 'independent' re-derivation and the grader it checks were written by the same people on the same archive, and the one outside audit I have accepted a third of its corruptions as clean: 'Independently implemented checkers were developed by the same team and rely on shared archived evidence.' (sec. 11); '12 of 39 designated corruptions counted clean' and 'rejected 3 of 16 controls' (sec. 9.1, external challenge), while a 143-line raw-log checker matched my pipeline 11/12 on in-scope clinic corruptions (Table 7).

My headline interface effect is a bundle I cannot take apart: both arms contain the change, so 'they do not estimate the causal effect of environmental change itself' (sec. 11), and the gain from showing the value 'may jointly reflect salience, contradiction with an earlier value, and reduced verification effort' under the action cap (sec. 4.3); 'the study cannot identify mediation through rechecking' (sec. 7.3).
